So, the first difference is that tropical cyclones are large systems. They can span up to a thousand miles in diameter. They are large and very organized. Tornadoes are small. They can be up to a mile in diameter, but they are very small. So, the first difference is scale. The second difference is that tropical cyclones are driven by a pressure system. Tornadoes are driven by a wind system. So, in a tropical cyclone, you have a pressure difference. You have low pressure in the center and high pressure around the center. That pressure difference makes air move in, and it also makes air move up. That makes clouds form. So, it is pressure-driven. Whereas tornadoes are wind-driven. So, in a tornado, you have a wind field that is very intense, very organized, and it is rotating. And that rotation is what makes the tornado. So, tornadoes are a wind phenomenon, and tropical cyclones are a pressure phenomenon. Now, you ask about the different names. So, we have hurricanes, we have typhoons, we have cyclones, we have tropical storms. They are all the same thing. They are all tropical cyclones. The only difference is where they occur. So, if you are in the Atlantic or the Eastern Pacific, we call it a hurricane. If you are in the Western Pacific, we call it a typhoon. If you are in the Southern Hemisphere, for example, Australia, New Zealand, or the Indian Ocean, we call it a cyclone. So, it is just a regional name. And then there are tropical storms, which are just weaker versions of a hurricane. So, a hurricane is a tropical cyclone that reaches a certain intensity. A tropical storm is a tropical cyclone that has not yet reached that intensity. So, the only difference is intensity. And then there are super typhoons, super hurricanes, or super cyclones, which are just the strongest versions of them.
